title: Lockout/Tagout for Electrically Powered Equipment
summary: Dozens of construction workers die every year because equipment was not turned off or locked out before work. Most are electrocuted, and some are crushed or lose limbs.
talking_points: Lockout/tagout protects workers while equipment is serviced. The person doing the work disconnects it, locks the power source, and puts on a warning tag so it cannot start up or release energy.
Before maintenance, identify every energy source to lock out and tag out: electrical, mechanical, gravitational, thermal, hydraulic, pneumatic, and chemical.
Apply a lock to the energy source so power cannot restart the equipment. Tell your co-workers about the shutdown. Put a tag on the locked-out item warning that it must not be turned on.
Test or look to make sure the energy source is really shut down and the item is locked out.
Block or drain any stored energy.
Equipment marked "high voltage" can store lethal energy, even when it is disconnected from the power source.
When work is done, tell co-workers the locks are about to come off and the equipment will restart. As the final step, remove the tag.
In one case, a worker cleaning the unguarded side of an operating band saw that had not been shut down was pulled into a nip point and died.
site_hazards_to_check: Equipment being serviced with no lock or tag on the power source
Energy sources not identified, such as hydraulic, pneumatic, or gravity
Stored energy not blocked or drained
Equipment marked "high voltage" that is treated as safe once unplugged
Unguarded moving parts on equipment that is still running
Co-workers who do not know equipment is locked out
discussion_questions: What energy sources does this equipment have, and how do we lock out each one?
How do we test that the equipment is really off before we start?
Who removes the lock and tag, and who do they tell first?
